svg.title: Three ways models share context: raw re-prefill, Plato's Key, and Speculative Encoding
svg.desc: Compares three ways heterogeneous models share a long document. Raw text re-prefill runs full O(N) prefill on every model. Stanford Plato's Key uses a closed-form Procrustes rotation plus global scale to prove latent states align geometrically without gradients. Ramp Labs Speculative Encoding uses a learned 2.35B MoE translator to convert hidden states directly, claiming up to 7.5x prefill speedup at 96.9% single-hop retention, while multi-hop chains still need verification.

g.text: Same-model prefix cache fails when two agents run different model families.
Model A reads doc → sends raw text → Model B re-prefills all tokens
100% native baseline accuracy · pays full N × prefill latency on swarms
Closed-form Procrustes rotation + 1 scale (zero gradient descent)
Proves spaces align: 41% median swap (vs 55% self), ~99% A→B→C chaining
Model A hidden states → 2.35B MoE translator → Model B KV/states
Reported: 96.9% acc, up to 7.5× prefill speedup · watch 0.969^k hop drift
